headline: AI Slack agent Centaur open-sourced, sharing lessons from the AI coworker space
summary: Centaur, an AI agent for Slack, now open-source, has been handling judgment-heavy tasks and codebase searches for 100-150 daily power users across multiple organizations.
details: Centaur, an AI agent for Slack originally built for internal investing and engineering work, has been open-sourced. It currently serves 100-150 daily power users across several organizations, handling complex tasks like investment research and extensive codebase searches.

The decision to open-source was driven by observations that most SaaS tools lack the customization and critical integrations companies require. External organizations using Centaur consistently reported these needs, highlighting a gap in the market.

Future development includes scoping Slackbot access by channel, which will enable safer multi-organizational collaboration within the same Slack space. A key challenge is maintaining low costs while ensuring the agent remains self-hostable for smaller teams.

The developers believe Slack is the optimal environment for coworker agents to thrive, rather than standalone applications. This approach allows for deeper integration into existing workflows and fosters a more natural interaction model for AI assistants.

Future development includes scoping Slackbot access by channel, which will enable safer multi-organizational collaboration within the same Slack space. A key challenge is maintaining low costs while ensuring the agent remains self-hostable for smaller teams.

The developers believe Slack is the optimal environment for coworker agents to thrive, rather than standalone applications. This approach allows for deeper integration into existing workflows and fosters a more natural interaction model for AI assistants.
